reason: src/main/local/agent-control.ts derives an encoded attachment limit from ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES; it does not call the module's image sniffing or journal matching. Stock needs those routines; the page uses MAIL_CUSTOM_TYPE to render mail.

session-pace.ts runs checkKinds(command, true) on the journal pages read by sessions.pacePage. The same shell grammar classifies grouped checks in renderer/work-checks.ts and stock's Autopilot. A second parser in Rust would let the work card and the pace report disagree (§1.3d).
src/main/omp-launch.ts imports CREDIT_SPEND_ENV to construct the child environment, not planSpentUntil or holdsCredits. Credit availability and payload decisions in this module run in stock.

src/main/desktop-slot.ts supplies DESKTOP_SLOT_LEASE_MS as a default lease argument. This file declares state, durations and notice strings, not lease arbitration; stock uses the idle duration and notices.
src/main/omp-launch.ts imports GH_GUARD_ENV and GH_BIN_DIR for launch wiring. The host does not call classify, watchArgs or parseRateLimit from this module; those belong to the child-side gh guard.
src/main/omp-launch.ts sets KEEP_CLI_ENV to the CLI path. The stock bridge, not the Node launcher, calls keepable, keptJobDir, keptExit and keptResult.

src/main/mcp-hub.ts sets the MCP_HUB_ENV key and src/main/ai-memory/service.ts passes MEMORY_HUB_ENTRY as configuration. These are env names and endpoint templates consumed by the launched MCP configuration, not listener or authentication logic.

src/main/model-setup-runner.ts builds a prompt whose shared formatter reads the ROLE_GROUPS table. Stock calls compactModelRoles; the page RPC client calls expandModelRoles. Main imports timeout utilities from that client, not its getModelRoles method.
local/auto-mode.ts waits AUTO_MODE_TIMEOUT_MS + 1000 for stock's decision; stock and the page also use the timing contract. The constant has no I/O (§1.3b,d).

Hub's spawn-bound dispatcher owns local/auto-mode.ts's noDecision fallback. Failure applying a decision retains its latency and model; failure reading it does not. Stock still uses noDecision for its classifier, and the page keeps the synchronous prompt guards (§1.3b,d).

Hub: autoTitleFromPrefs defaults launch settings; titleSuppressedByEnv checks PI_NO_TITLE. Shell: synchronous PREFS_SET accepts only booleans for both switches (§1.3a,b,c). Stock and the page keep the title and settings contract. Live updates keep the launch-time PI_NO_TITLE bit from the process and login-shell environments.

src/main/autopilot.ts calls shipPolicyForPreset to derive push/release permissions; it uses withRecentCycles to send only the newest 30 cycles with the full count. Preserve those host decisions; stock and page still exchange the status and presets.
src/main/autopilot-approver.ts calls findBanViolation on the proposed action card before approval. Move that approval boundary with the host approver; stock still enforces the live tool boundary.

CheckoutPeerCoordinator judges fresh bridge and Git facts before publishing the same per-tab peers agent-control reads to authorize reports. §1.3(b,d): judgeClaim does no I/O; stock's tool_call must claim before allowing the tool and settle the same owner/call on tool_result. Receiver: the checkout pass with its ordered bridge publisher.

src/main/checkout-peers.ts sends CHECKOUT_RETIRE and CHECKOUT_STATUS; sidecar-factory recognizes CHECKOUT_FILES_EVENT. These are wire names, not the judgeClaim decision. Stock and page still use the peer protocol.

src/main/agent-desktop.ts writes COMPUTER_USE_ENV after calling a preference parser from src/shared/computer-use.ts. This bridge module supplies launch names and the tool prefix; stock parses its environment and the page reads notices.
Hub batch: omp-launch uses agentBrowserEnv to encode the selected relay as relay:<name>@<url> at launch. Stock decodes it; the page keeps the selection contract.

Hub: sidecar-factory defaults invalid modes at launch. Shell: PREFS_SET rejects invalid writes with the same isDelegationMode as stock and the page; a separate validator duplicates the vocabulary without moving the store (§1.3b,d). Live delegation is per session.

Hub: only false disables judge assist at launch. Shell: notification triage reads the same rule, but writes require a boolean before synchronous persistence and live fan-out (§1.3a,c). Stock and the page keep the judge contract. Preview and memory care read the current preference too.
The Rust corpus builder calls the Bun stock worker for contentTerms. The live extension uses the same tokenizer to score recall; Node no longer builds document frequencies.

Hub: nextPromptFromPrefs defaults non-booleans to true at launch. Shell: both switches require boolean writes before synchronous persistence and notification (§1.3a,c). Local request validation keeps the draft, child and refresh limits; stock and the page keep the suggestion contract. Live updates and stock’s environment decoder use the same switch defaults.
src/main/omp-launch.ts imports SCRATCH_ENV to pass the directory. It does not call scratchSection; stock renders that prompt section.
session-summaries and agent-control derive the displayed assignment from the current messages. The renderer reads the same assignment headline; extracting a string has no independent I/O (§1.3b,d).

Hub: sidecar-factory trims valid names and drops invalid fields at launch. Shell: PREFS_SET checks isUserProfile, measuring trimmed UTF-16 length but storing a valid name untrimmed; a separate write parser duplicates the stock/page contract (§1.3d). Settings and stock share the launch and live profile normalizer.
src/main/index.ts joins OMPDESK_ROLES_FILE to userData and omp-launch.ts exports the path under OMPDESK_ROLES_ENV. Stock's ompdesk-roles.ts, not main, calls parseRolePicks and heldRoleValue.

atomic-file.ts's synchronous writer must finish rename before returning; its deferred writer starts a save before returning its cancellation function. Stock's MCP config writer shares the Windows retry policy. Move the writer with its callers, not the error predicate or delays (§1.3a,c,d).

src/shared/restart-cuts.ts consumes three RESTART_*_MESSAGE names for main session summaries and the page. Main's process-shape imports are type-only; interruptedJobs and stoppedSubagents are stock journal computations, not host calls.

frame-bookkeeping removes request metadata before delivering a frame; local/extensions projects stock's transcript after checking the journal tail. Projection alone would send the entire transcript across the wire to repeat stock's shared rule (§1.3a,b,d).

src/main/model-wait-count.ts aliases LATE_FIRST_OUTPUT_MS and turn-stages-log.ts imports TURN_STAGES_EVENT. The threshold and event vocabulary cross host, stock and page; this module does not measure elapsed time or count waits.

session-pace.ts folds createPollTracker.observe across journal pages and uses waitWindowElapsed on wait results. Stock uses the same poll history and wait rules to issue live hints. Keep one classifier for old journals and live tools; the core reads the journal, not a second set of guard rules (§1.3d).

Hub owns sidecar-factory's launch choice and account-rotation.ts's live update after a write; machine-services reads and sets the local mode. Shell owns ipc.ts write validation. The page uses the same mode list; parsing alone has no I/O (§1.3b,d). Launch defaults an absent or invalid mode to quota.

agent-control/host reads current prefs synchronously to grant capabilities. Turn resume and paired hosts parse agent mail; the page uses the same message and review vocabulary. Move authorization with its owner and do not reimplement the shared parser (§1.3a,c,d).

§1.3(d): the editor and local/agent-files share agentNameError, agentFileName and serializeAgentMarkdown before live stock validation. fs.agentFile separately enforces direct filenames and authorized directories at the mutation boundary.

§1.3(d): the gallery and local/agent-files need the same templateDraft defaults and serialization before live stock validation; copying the catalog to Rust would create a second template source. fs.agentFile installs validated bytes without overwriting.

AI_MEMORY_BINARIES, AI_MEMORY_VERSION and the build-manifest name supply package metadata to main/ai-memory/service.ts; MemoryPages.tsx uses AI_MEMORY_KINDS. The shared module does not start the binary or implement memory operations.
session-summaries decodes async-result messages in its summary pass. The page also decodes them for transcript cards; extracting jobs has no independent I/O (§1.3b,d).

Autopilot's prText callback and AutopilotCycles copy the same title/body from recorded cycles. Formatting the report does no Git or network I/O and duplicating the formatter could change the copied text (§1.3b,d).
BRIDGE_HEALTH_GET is only the channel name "bridge-health:get", used by main/ipc.ts and main/web/ipc-policy.ts. There is no health check implementation here and no page runtime caller is required.
Shell updater batch, §1.3a,d: isCliToolId validates the requested update before queuing it. CliUpdateRows uses the same tool names and update-state contract for display.
setup.pickAgentDesktop already probes the executable. main/agent-desktop.ts and the settings row use the same preference parser for builtin versus agent-desktop; the parser does no I/O (§1.3b,d).

main/control-socket/index.ts publishes CONTROL_PROTOCOL_VERSION and endpoint.ts uses POSIX_SOCKET_FILE. These are socket wire/discovery constants; isControlResponse has no production caller found. No page runtime dependency or socket implementation here.

machine-services reads and writes the local switch; shell's PREFS_SET and machine.setCreditSpend reject non-booleans before writing. Hub launch and guarded model calls recheck the pref: only true permits spending. The page keeps CREDIT_SPEND_OFF_WORDING (§1.3a,c,d). Bridge updates, scheduled launches and machine status also read the current gate.

browsers.status supplies the automatic choice. Hub's sidecar-factory applies the explicit pref or relay and needs the named Chromium even when the launch read expires (§1.3c). Shell's PREFS_SET validates Settings vocabulary, not current availability. The page keeps the catalog, pref parser and status contract (§1.3d).

main/index.ts combines tray availability with closeToTrayEnabled, which defaults on unless the stored value is false. Move close behavior to the Rust window owner; GeneralSection and update settings still need the preference keys.
The host imports archive contracts and the diagnostics member name. app.diagnosticBundleFileName formats its default path in Rust; the paired browser formats its own save-dialog suggestion locally.

The page displays the same age thresholds the host passes to disk.scratchIdle and checks under the live worktree removal claim. §1.3(c,d): keep one value for the displayed policy and the owner deciding admission; move the host check with that claim, not as a second independent cleanup rule.

Hub's sidecar-factory enables the extension unless the stored value is false. Startup's agent-power-migration reads ECC_PREF; EccRow writes it through generic PREFS_SET, with no ECC-specific write check. The key has no independent I/O (§1.3b,d). builtinMcp samples it before its first await. The roots apply to both tab kinds, the prompt only to agents. Move with launch assembly before Windows quoting (§1.3b).
main/i18n.ts and renderer/lib/i18n.tsx synchronously fill the same placeholders and plural slots. Formatting a message does no I/O (§1.3a,b,d).

local/git/exec.ts and autopilot.ts strip inherited selectors when building the child's environment, before applying caller overrides. Repository scripts share withoutGitSelectors. It does not spawn Git; core already owns git/gh execution (§1.3b,d).
Shell sign-in batch, §1.3a,d: GithubAuthService clears or keeps the current flow synchronously using githubLoginLive; GithubSignIn reads the same states for presentation.

local/git/github.ts validates the request with shared host/repo patterns before resolving gh. The page uses them for form errors. A second validator in the core could change error precedence and would duplicate the page rule (§1.3b,d).

save-copy.ts decodes the peer's error before falling back only on unsupported. Page handlers use the same wire decoding. That decoder does no I/O; file copy and remote reads belong to their own operations (§1.3b,d).

IPC_COMMANDS, IPC_EVENTS, HOST_UPDATE_ACTIONS and transfer-size constants are runtime wire data alongside erased interfaces. Main dispatch and page/preload clients need matching values; the module itself does not dispatch commands or enforce limits.
KEYCHAIN_WOULD_ASK is the shared failure marker, used by main/update-auth.ts and UpdatesSection.tsx. It neither accesses the keychain nor decides whether prompting is allowed.

Shell prefs and hub session launch batches, §1.3a,d: launch-profile-store reads SafeStore synchronously; sidecar and omp-launch filter flags on spawn. LaunchSettings shares profileToFlags and flagsToCommandLine for its preview.

Shell models editor, §1.3a,c: index.ts reads registered/removed from one SafeStore ledger; machine-services shares its default-on rule. Core probes the endpoint selected by LocalEngineDetector; move the ledger with provider mutations, not a second owner.
Shell IPC batch, §1.3a,d: ipc.ts rejects unknown grant names before dispatch. MacPermissionFix uses the same MAC_PERMISSIONS vocabulary to show missing grants; the signed app owns the OS calls.

mailAccountProblem validates both immediate dialog feedback and saves against the account's current hasPassword, including a blocked keystore. §1.3(c,d): the synchronous resolve/state caller and the page share this validator. Move host validation with account ownership, not with the IMAP connection.

remote/devices.ts checks allowedLogin against the live preferences before committing and returning sidebar-rank exchanges, not just on first admission. Moving that check alone introduces an await after authorization (§1.3a,c). Keep webDeviceTier, grant presets and channel contracts with their page consumers.
omp/rename.rs recognizes stock's restore failure for an offline rename. Sidecar startup and the page's switch-session recovery still read parseModelRestoreFailure synchronously.

Shell and paired-host model setup handlers, §1.3d: ModelSetupRunner and the page share request validation and returned-plan parsing. Core runs the generated research prompt; do not add another schema.
web-push-notifier and renderer use-rpc-events format the same notification body. Removing Markdown and truncating text does no I/O; move delivery independently of the shared formatter (§1.3b,d).

Exports update-state types, OMP_UPDATE_FAILURE_REASONS and the six-hour VERIFYING_OVERDUE_MS value. remote/app-protocol.ts consumes the vocabulary and the page the same update contract; the core's tools kind decides whether to notify or install.

preview/agent-relay.ts checks URLs before navigating a live page; the renderer also uses previewUrl and isLoopbackUrl before offering a URL. Keep the shared rules until the shell preview takes the navigation and page identity together (§1.3a,d).

PRODUCT_REPO is the repository identifier and PRODUCT_REPO_URL its derived URL. github-auth/service.ts consumes these values (the shell's app menu spells the URL itself, tauri-shell/src/app_menu.rs); keep them available to the page. There is no repository-selection or network behavior here.

Local git/project.rs derives and caches checkout identity; the local client shares worktree kind and slug naming with the page (§1.3d). On session_folder_missing, RemoteSidecar.#bringUp checks isOmpdeskWorktreeFolder before emitting folderGone or setting error. Move that check with the device-side reply (§1.3a,b,d). The page keeps worktreeKindOf, autopilotRunOf and worktreeLabel for the sidebar and title bar.

Hub's sidecar-factory includes the pack unless the stored value is false. Startup's agent-power-migration reads PSTACK_PREF; PstackRow writes it through generic PREFS_SET, with no pstack-specific write check. The key has no independent I/O (§1.3b,d). builtinMcp samples it before its first await. The roots apply to both tab kinds, the prompt only to agents. Move with launch assembly before Windows quoting (§1.3b).

Autopilot checks isLimitWording while observing the current turn and quotaWaitUntil chooses the earliest future reset only if all matching accounts are limited, otherwise 15 minutes. Core resume already calculates quota_wait_until; move with the cycle, not a second RPC for timestamp math. The page uses quotaResetAt for display (§1.3b,d).

Hub: sidecar-factory resolves auto against the device language at launch; stock receives the resolved name. Shell: PREFS_SET validates against Settings' language choices before writing (§1.3d); a second list would drift. Live pushes resolve the current device language again; diagnostics and SYSTEM_INFO read its tag synchronously.

SessionSummaries derives roster state from restart notes for current() before publishing. Page work cards and subagent views interpret the same cuts. No I/O here; move host interpretation with roster ownership.

diagnostic-bundle.ts selects timeoutForCommand before issuing the dump and remote host services enforce the timeout bound. The page client uses the same command table; a native lookup alone would not own a request or its deadline.

SidecarManager dispatches live frames; SidecarPool and agent-control/host classify blocking vs sign-in requests before routing them. The page consumes those same vocabularies; the tables do no I/O and moving them alone duplicates a wire rule.

Remote-web moves ScheduleFrequencySchema, ScheduleEventSchema and ScheduleRunSchema with remote/app-protocol.ts; no page runtime caller. The peer decoder bounds remote drafts, strips local-only wakeSession, and checks replies and host.schedules.changed. RemoteClient matches a reply by id, and RemoteDevices broadcasts each validated change before a subsequent reply. Move both with ordered link dispatch (§1.3a,c,d).

Rust validates every saved draft; the page still checks the same draft for immediate feedback. Run counts and chain limits reach schedules.open from the host. Production trigger polling and source validation now run in core; the wire types remain shared.

SessionListShare.#publish compares and replaces its numbered copy without yielding; HostSessionList.hostChanged reads held() to validate a delta base. The page applies the same ordering and delta contract. Move with host copy ownership.

SessionSummaries.current flushes the pending roster before returning; diffSummaries is part of the same publication. Keep its host use with that roster, and the page's hostedSummaries, unsavedSessionKey and summaryAgentSnapshot in the shared contract.

SessionTarget and SessionArtwork are wire shapes; SESSION_TARGET_BATCH is the shared value 24. main/session-targets.ts enforces it in request schemas and page clients batch requests against it. No Git lookup or artwork discovery runs in this module.
Shell setup batch, §1.3a,d: SetupService and setup IPC synchronously select required items and validate retry IDs; page setup/update views share the item vocabulary and state contract.

updateSidebarPrefs reads, patches and saves the current host preference without yielding. The page also normalizes the preference and applies sidebar changes; port the host use with its store, not by reproducing sidebarPatch in a second language.

SidebarProjects initializes state from parseSidebarProjects before index.ts exposes state() to local and paired snapshots. The page consumes the project and layout contract. There is no separately awaited file operation here.

SidebarLayoutScope classifies a chat before applying a reorder; routines/sessions.ts uses openerOfSessions to match session ancestry. Both consume the page's row rules synchronously. Keep those uses with their owners rather than duplicating the renderer's rules.

Exports SSH_TOOLS_* channels, request/state shapes and numeric grace, polling and prompt limits. main/ssh/client.ts and service.ts implement SSH behavior; the settings page needs the contract. No connection, retry or prompt handling executes in this file.

main/startup-timing.ts calls isRendererStartupMark before recording a mark; it admits only renderer-mounted, first-run-check and first-run-visible. Move this host ingress check with startup timing. The renderer sends names but is not a runtime importer in the recorded graph.

TerminalOperation and TerminalSnapshot are wire types; TERMINAL_POLL_MAX_WAIT_MS and TERMINAL_OUTPUT_BUDGET are protocol limits. main/terminal/requests.ts applies them in validTerminalOperation. The page needs the contract and the stock PTY helper imports its types; no operation validator or PTY code lives here.

main/index.ts and window-chrome.ts use migrateThemeName to map retired stored IDs to current selections. Port the host preference/chrome decision; renderer/lib/themes.ts independently resolves saved and system themes for the page.

AutopilotApprover, the pool and paired host inspect the current card before deciding who may answer it. The page uses approvalChoices to present that same card. Classification has no independent I/O (§1.3a,c,d).
main/i18n.ts uses isUiLanguage and uiLanguageFromLocale to select the host language; main/ipc.ts validates the preference. Keep UI language names, locale mappings and cycling for page controls.

main/omp-updater.ts uses isNewer and majorOf, and main/update-release.ts uses compareVersions to recheck the minimum Darwin version. Port host version decisions; renderer settings rows and RemoteSection also compare versions for display.

WEB_HOST_CHANNELS, WEB_DEVICE_CHANNELS, the 500-entry response cap and request/result shapes are the paired page contract. main/web/host-actions.ts implements the operations; there is no filesystem access or host action implementation in the shared file.

WsRouter.#dispatch uses holdsBlock and isWebUploadedImage before its first await: plain calls reach the registry in arrival order, while uploaded references go through the device-owned UploadStore and stock conversion. Pairing uses DEFAULT_WEB_GRANTS. Keep the page's block predicates and grant presets shared; moving predicates alone would insert an await or duplicate them (§1.3a,d).

main/web/devices-store.ts-61 consumes DEFAULT_WEB_PUSH_SETTINGS as data. The executable notificationOpenUrl helper is used by renderer/web/sw-core.ts for notification clicks; the settings page needs WEB_PUSH_CATEGORIES. Host delivery and settings application live outside this file.

local/git/worktree.ts validates the stored or requested prefix before branch creation. WorktreeDialog and WorktreeBranchPrefixRow check the same rule before submitting; prefix validation has no I/O (§1.3b,d).
